name: Docker
scope:
A person with ADVANCED proficiency level in Docker as a competency should be able to explain and manipulate the full OCI stack—Docker CLI, dockerd, containerd, runc, Linux namespaces, cgroups, seccomp—while knowing where BuildKit, Swarm, OCI Image / Distribution / Runtime specs plug in.  
They design highly optimised multi-stage, multi-platform BuildKit pipelines with secrets, inline cache and metadata, choose minimal-or-full hardened base images, generate SBOMs, sign provenance via cosign/Notary v2 and drive CVE remediation.  
They run and secure private registries such as Harbor, Artifactory, ECR, ACR, GCR or registry v2 with Content-Trust, geo-replication, retention and GC policies.  
They architect multi-host networking using bridge, overlay VXLAN (encrypted mesh), MACVLAN/IPVLAN, host/none drivers, DNS, service-discovery, IPVS load-balancing, ingress routing, dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 and integrate with external SDN/CNI, troubleshooting via tcpdump, wireshark, iptables/nftables, conntrack.  
They choose and tune storage drivers overlay2, fuse-overlayfs, devmapper-thin, ZFS, Btrfs; design persistent data with volumes, bind-mounts, tmpfs, NFS, CIFS, Flocker, Portworx, EBS/EFS or CSI, automate backup/DR, encryption-at-rest and measure with iostat, fio, blkio stats.  
They enforce runtime security through rootless mode, capability trimming, read-only FS, seccomp-bpf, AppArmor/SELinux, masked paths, user-namespace remap, integrate Trivy/Grype/Anchore scanners, OPA/Gatekeeper/Docker Policy Engine, CIS Benchmark, NIST 800-190, manage secrets via Swarm secrets, KMS, Vault or cloud managers, and implement Sigstore (cosign, Rekor) plus SLSA attestations.  
They operate Swarm or feed Kubernetes, Nomad, ECS/Fargate with Compose v2 stacks using extension fields, profiles, rollbacks, secrets/configs, placement constraints and health orchestration, while running HA control-planes, automated node lifecycle, zero-downtime upgrades and multi-region fail-over.  
They wire observability with cadvisor/node-exporter to Prometheus, Datadog, InfluxDB or CloudWatch, centralise logs via json-file, syslog, fluentd, gelf, awslogs, splunk, consume the Docker event stream, debug using exec, nsenter, gdb, strace, ltrace, sysdig, perf, bcc, bpftrace, analyse cgroup pressure, core dumps and layer checksums, and tune cpu-shares/cpuset, blkio weights, memory limits, hugepages, ulimits.  
They build end-to-end CI/CD with GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Tekton, Argo-CD to compile, test, scan, sign and push images, promote via immutable tags/semantic versions, accelerate inner-loop via Docker-Compose, DevContainer, tilt or telepresence, and exploit build caches and dependency proxies.  
They guide architectural choices on microservices vs monolith, sidecars, service-mesh, multi-tenancy, cost models, publish guidelines, review checklists, base-image lifecycles, run risk and capacity assessments, cost-optimisation and incident post-mortems.  
They mentor others, author runbooks and reusable Compose/base-image templates, track emerging tech like rootless Docker, buildpacks, WASM containers, eBPF isolation, stargz/nydus snapshotters, and liaise with InfoSec, SRE, QA, auditors and executives to align container strategy with business goals.
long_scope:
COMPETENCY: DOCKER – ADVANCED PROFICIENCY (≈ 6–10 years of focused, production-grade experience)

Scope = the entire body of knowledge, skills and behaviours that an individual at this level is expected to control and apply with confidence in day-to-day engineering work.  The scope is expressed as capabilities that must be demonstrated, the depth at which concepts must be understood, and the outcomes that have to be delivered on complex, real-world systems.

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Mental Model & Internal Architecture
────────────────────────────────────────
• Maintains a clear, low-level mental model of the OCI stack: Docker CLI → dockerd → containerd → runc → Linux kernel namespaces / cgroups / seccomp.  
• Understands how images, layers, manifests and content-addressable storage work; can reason about the on-disk image graph, layer deduplication and garbage-collection processes.  
• Appreciates the design boundaries between Docker-specific components (BuildKit, Swarm) and generic container standards (OCI Image Spec, Distribution Spec, Runtime Spec).

Outcome: Can predict how a change in one layer (e.g., changing the storage driver, enabling rootless mode) will propagate through the rest of the stack, and can plan mitigations up-front.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Image Construction, Build Engineering & Supply Chain
────────────────────────────────────────
• Designs and maintains highly optimised, reproducible, hermetic image build processes using multi-stage builds, BuildKit secrets, inline cache export/import, multi-platform targets and build metadata annotations.  
• Establishes organisation-wide base-image strategy: minimal vs. full, distro choice, hardening, SBOM generation, provenance signing (cosign / Notary v2), and systematic vulnerability remediation workflows.  
• Operates private registries at scale (Harbor, Artifactory, ECR, ACR, GCR, or self-hosted registry v2 with Content Trust), including replication, geo-mirrors, garbage-collection schedules, retention policies and SLA monitoring.  

Outcome: Image build pipelines are fast, deterministic, CVE-managed, auditable, and support multi-arch releases without developer friction.

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Networking Design & Operations
────────────────────────────────────────
• Engineers multi-host networking topologies using bridge, overlay (VXLAN, encrypted mesh), MACVLAN/IPVLAN, host and none drivers; can explain control-plane vs. data-plane mechanics, packet flow and MTU implications.  
• Configures embedded DNS, service discovery, load-balancing, ingress routing, dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 support and user-defined network isolation strategies; integrates with external SDN or CNI solutions when required.  
• Performs live traffic debugging with tcpdump/wireshark, iptables/nftables tracing, conntrack and IPVS inspection inside container namespaces.

Outcome: Distributed container workloads communicate reliably across datacentres/VPCs with appropriate encryption, isolation, fault-tolerance and observability.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Volume & Filesystem Management
────────────────────────────────────────
• Selects and configures storage drivers (overlay2, fuse-overlayfs, devicemapper-thin, ZFS, Btrfs) based on workload and kernel version; quantifies trade-offs in copy-on-write performance, inode pressure and snapshot semantics.  
• Implements data persistence through local volumes, bind mounts, tmpfs, NFS, CIFS, Flocker, Portworx, Amazon EBS/EFS, or cloud-native CSI plugins; automates backup/restore, encryption-at-rest and disaster-recovery playbooks.  
• Tunes filesystem and I/O parameters (direct I/O, commit, journaling mode, trim, async) and monitors latency/throughput using iostat, fio and container-granular blkio stats.

Outcome: Stateful services achieve predictable durability and performance without sacrificing container portability.

────────────────────────────────────────
5. Runtime Security & Compliance
────────────────────────────────────────
• Enforces least-privilege execution via rootless containers, Linux capabilities trimming, read-only FS, seccomp-bpf filters, AppArmor / SELinux policies, masked paths, TMPDIR controls and user namespace remapping.  
• Integrates image scanning (Trivy, Grype, Anchore), policy engines (OPA / Gatekeeper, Docker Policy Engine) and compliance frameworks (CIS Docker Benchmark, NIST 800-190) into CI pipelines and production admission flows.  
• Manages secrets and sensitive configurations through Docker Swarm secrets, external KMS, HashiCorp Vault, or cloud secret managers; rotates credentials and ensures in-memory only exposure.  
• Implements software supply-chain assurance with Sigstore (cosign, Rekor transparency log), SLSA levels and attestation verification at deploy time.

Outcome: Production clusters pass security audits and continuous assurance gates with evidence, while remaining developer-friendly.

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Orchestration & Distributed Operations
────────────────────────────────────────
• Operates Docker Swarm or integrates Docker-built images seamlessly into Kubernetes, Nomad or ECS/Fargate; can contrast scheduler architectures, overlay networks, service primitives, rolling-update semantics and failure domains.  
• Authoritative on docker stack/compose v2 specification: extension fields, profiles, rollbacks, canonical layouts, secrets/configs, placement constraints and condition-based health orchestration.  
• Designs high-availability control-plane architectures, automated node lifecycle management, zero-downtime upgrades, and multi-region fail-over strategies.  

Outcome: Containers are scheduled, updated and recovered automatically with predictable blast radius and minimal manual intervention.

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Observability, Debugging & Performance Tuning
────────────────────────────────────────
• Exposes per-container metrics (CPU/mem/kernel, blkio, network, pids, oom events) and forwards them to Prometheus, Datadog, InfluxDB, or CloudWatch; configures cadvisor / node-exporter and uses Docker event stream for alerting.  
• Centralises structured logs via logging drivers (json-file, syslog, fluentd, gelf, awslogs, splunk) and correlates them through trace IDs or OpenTelemetry contexts.  
• Executes systematic incident analysis: container exec/debug, nsenter, gdb/strace/ltrace/sysdig, perf/BPF tools (bcc, bpftrace), cgroup pressure analysis, core-dump extraction and layer checksum validation.  
• Tunes resource controls—cpu shares, cpuset, blkio weights, memory limits, hugepages, ulimits—and runs load tests to validate SLO compliance.

Outcome: Performance anomalies and production incidents are detected early, diagnosed quickly and resolved with permanent fixes.

────────────────────────────────────────
8. Continuous Delivery, GitOps & Developer Experience
────────────────────────────────────────
• Constructs end-to-end CI/CD flows (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Tekton, Argo-CD) that compile, test, scan, sign and push images; manages promotion between environments through immutable tags, semantic versioning and release channels.  
• Implements local-dev parity through Docker-Compose/DevContainer or tilt/telepresence, accelerating inner-loop development while keeping parity with production base images and runtime flags.  
• Uses build caches, dependency proxies and parallel build matrices to minimise pipeline duration and infrastructure cost.  

Outcome: Teams iterate rapidly with confidence; every commit can be traced to a signed image running in a known environment.

────────────────────────────────────────
9. Architecture, Governance & Best Practices
────────────────────────────────────────
• Guides architectural decisions on micro-services vs. monolith trade-offs, sidecars vs. helper containers, service mesh implications, multi-tenancy boundaries and cost models.  
• Defines coding & container guidelines, review checklists, base-image life-cycle calendars, deprecation processes, sunset communication plans and cross-team RFC procedures.  
• Leads risk assessments, capacity planning, cost optimisation (rightsizing, spot fleets, registry egress fees) and incident post-mortems, converting learnings into revised standards and automation.  

Outcome: Organisation-wide Docker usage is coherent, cost-efficient, maintainable and aligned with larger business & compliance objectives.

────────────────────────────────────────
10. Leadership & Knowledge Sharing
────────────────────────────────────────
• Mentors engineers from beginner to intermediate levels, runs internal workshops, writes high-quality documentation, creates reusable compose files, base image templates and internal libraries/modules.  
• Evaluates emerging container trends and tools (e.g., rootless Docker, buildpacks, WASM containers, eBPF-based isolation, snapshotters like stargz/nydus) and presents actionable adoption roadmaps.  
• Interfaces confidently with InfoSec, SRE, QA, compliance auditors and executive stakeholders, translating technical constraints and improvements into business terms.

Outcome: Team maturity and delivery velocity increase due to shared understanding, clear patterns and proactive adoption of vetted innovations.

────────────────────────────────────────
Boundary to Next Levels
────────────────────────────────────────
An Advanced practitioner is self-sufficient on all the above, can run large production fleets and can introduce new patterns responsibly.  An Expert goes beyond by contributing to upstream projects, designing novel container runtimes, or running fleets at hyperscale (tens of thousands of nodes) and shaping industry-wide best practices.

────────────────────────────────────────
Deliverables & Evidence of Competence
────────────────────────────────────────
1. Production systems reference architectures, runbooks and post-mortems authored or co-owned.  
2. CI/CD pipelines, image repositories and security reports demonstrating reproducibility, compliance and SBOM coverage.  
3. Measurable improvements in deployment frequency, MTTR, resource utilisation and incident rates attributable to the engineer’s container strategies.  
4. Internal training material or workshops delivered, plus mentoring feedback.

────────────────────────────────────────
Summary
────────────────────────────────────────
At Advanced proficiency, the engineer is a dependable authority on Docker within the organisation.  They convert business requirements into stable, secure, observable and cost-optimised container solutions, anticipate edge-cases before they become incidents, and uplift colleagues through mentorship and coherent standards—while still recognising that deeper, cutting-edge research and community leadership distinguish the Expert tier.

name: Java
scope: A person with ADVANCED proficiency level in Java as a competency should be able to apply deep knowledge of OOP, concurrency (java.util.concurrent, ForkJoinPool, CompletableFuture), generics, streams, and advanced language features to design robust, high-performance systems. They can fine-tune garbage collectors (CMS, G1, ZGC, Shenandoah), analyze memory usage with tools like jmap and jstat, address bytecode-level optimizations, and orchestrate class loading. They structure complex enterprise applications or microservices with Spring (Boot, Data, Security, Cloud) or Jakarta EE (JPA, EJB, CDI), employing design patterns (Factory, Strategy, Observer, Repository, CQRS) and assessing trade-offs in distributed architectures. They practice advanced testing (JUnit, TestNG, Spring Boot integration) and mocking (Mockito, WireMock), use build tools (Maven, Gradle), and set up CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions) for automated, reliable deployments. They containerize (Docker, Kubernetes) and integrate systems on AWS, Azure, or GCP while addressing security via Spring Security, OAuth2, JWT, encryption, OWASP compliance, and role-based controls. They optimize data persistence with advanced JPA/Hibernate (second-level caching, lazy loading, Criteria API), handle concurrency pitfalls, and diagnose performance via profilers (YourKit, JProfiler, VisualVM). They manage integrations (REST, SOAP, JMS, or reactive messaging), tackle distributed transactions and fault tolerance, and maintain observability with logging, metrics, and tracing tools (Prometheus, ELK, Grafana, Jaeger). They mentor peers through code reviews, refine architectures for scalability, and keep applications modular and maintainable. They ensure compliance with regulatory standards (PCI-DSS, GDPR), maintain operational readiness for production, and troubleshoot complex production issues promptly. They configure pipelines for blue-green or canary deployments and adopt feature toggles for progressive rollouts. Finally, they stay abreast of Java releases (Project Loom, GraalVM), continuously refine performance, and contribute to technical excellence across teams.
long_scope:
Below is a comprehensive scope that captures the breadth and depth expected of someone with an ADVANCED proficiency in Java. This level typically reflects 6–10 years of hands-on experience. Such a professional is beyond the fundamentals and can tackle complex design and architectural problems, optimize systems at scale, and guide teams, but they may not exhibit the same level of specialized or novel expertise as an EXPERT with 10+ years of experience. The outline here groups key areas of mastery—concepts, frameworks, tools, and tasks—to give a holistic view. Each section clarifies the kind of knowledge, capabilities, and outcomes expected from an advanced Java developer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Language Mastery and Core API Proficiency
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• Deep Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) skills: Demonstrates fluent use of inheritance, encapsulation, polymorphism, and abstraction. Is well-versed in applying OOP principles to solve real-world problems and can critique and refine designs that deviate from best practices.  
• Advanced Language Features: Applies generics in high-complexity scenarios (e.g., designing reusable libraries), understands annotations (including custom annotation processing), and uses Java functional constructs (streams, lambdas) for clean, readable solutions while being conscious of performance implications.  
• Concurrency & Multithreading: Understands the Java Memory Model in depth and uses concurrent utilities (from java.util.concurrent, ForkJoinPool, CompletableFuture, etc.) to build high-performance, thread-safe applications. Can identify and address concurrency pitfalls such as deadlocks or race conditions, and can design robust concurrency solutions.  
• Collections & Data Structures: Has in-depth knowledge of the Java Collections Framework, understands the complexities (time, space) of different data structures, and can tailor them to large-scale data processing or memory-sensitive applications.  
• Platform Nuances & Versions: Stays updated with language evolution from older LTS releases to more recent versions; migrates legacy code from older versions to newer ones thoughtfully and knows how to leverage new features for performance or readability gains.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. JVM Internals and Memory Management
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• Garbage Collection & Tuning: Knows the architecture of various garbage collectors (Serial, Parallel, CMS, G1, ZGC, Shenandoah) and can analyze GC logs, tune GC parameters, and diagnose memory leaks using tools like jmap, jstat, and profilers.  
• Class Loading & Bytecode: Understands class loaders, class loading hierarchies, and can diagnose classpath conflicts. Has a conceptual understanding of bytecode manipulation (perhaps using libraries like ASM or ByteBuddy) for instrumentation or advanced proxying requirements.  
• Runtime Optimization: Can configure and tune JVM parameters (e.g., heap size, Metaspace settings, compiler flags) to optimize performance in production environments.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Software Architecture and System Design
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• Application Layering and Modular Design: Structures large-scale applications using layered architectures (presentation, business, data layers) or modular designs (OSGi, Java Platform Module System). Ensures loose coupling and high cohesion across modules.  
• Design Patterns & Best Practices: Routinely applies (and teaches) classic design patterns (e.g., Factory, Singleton, Strategy, Observer) and enterprise patterns (e.g., Dependency Injection, Repository, CQRS). Knows how to select patterns based on trade-offs and system constraints.  
• Distributed System Principles & Microservices Architecture: Builds cloud-native or microservices-based solutions, leveraging best practices—API gateways, load balancing, distributed transactions, fault tolerance patterns (circuit breakers, bulkheads), service discovery, etc.  
• Integration & Interoperability: Works comfortably integrating Java applications with other systems and technologies (REST, SOAP, messaging systems like JMS, or newer reactive messaging technologies). Handles data interoperability formats (JSON, XML, Avro) and asynchronous paradigms where needed.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Frameworks, Libraries, and Tooling
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• Core Enterprise Frameworks (Spring, Jakarta EE):  
  – Spring Ecosystem: Demonstrates advanced use of Spring Boot, Spring Data JPA, Spring Security, Spring Cloud (Eureka, Config Server, Circuit Breaker libraries), and understands core patterns (e.g., IoC, AOP).  
  – Jakarta EE: Comfortable with JPA, CDI, EJB, servlet containers, and more. Able to choose between Spring or Jakarta EE technologies based on project context.  
• Persistence & Database Interaction: Mastery of ORM frameworks (Hibernate, EclipseLink) and knowledge of advanced JPA features (e.g., second-level caching, lazy loading, advanced JPQL/Criteria API usage). Understands transaction handling and can optimize queries.  
• Build & Dependency Management: Proficient in Maven and Gradle, including advanced configurations (multi-module builds, custom plugins, build profiles) and managing large dependency graphs.  
• Team Tooling & Environments: Uses integrated developer environments (IDEs) like IntelliJ IDEA or Eclipse with advanced refactoring, debugging, and code analysis features. Is also capable with version control (Git), automated testing setups, and CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions).  
• Containerization & Cloud Platforms: Has practical knowledge of Docker (creating Dockerfiles, image optimization) and can deploy and orchestrate Java applications in Kubernetes or on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Testing, Quality Assurance, and Reliability
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• Testing Strategies and Frameworks: Designs comprehensive testing strategies that incorporate unit tests (JUnit/TestNG), integration tests (Spring Boot testing, Quarkus testing), contract tests, and end-to-end tests. Leverages mocking/proxying frameworks (Mockito, WireMock) effectively.  
• Test Automation & Coverage: Ensures continuous testing via CI pipelines and aims for high coverage without sacrificing maintainability. Guides junior engineers on TDD/BDD practices and automated regression suites.  
• Observability & Monitoring: Configures application logs, metrics, and distributed tracing (using tools like Prometheus, Grafana, ELK stack, Jaeger, Zipkin). Understands how to troubleshoot performance bottlenecks and error spikes in production using dashboards and alerts.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Performance Engineering and Optimization
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• Profiling & Diagnostics: Uses commercial/open-source profilers (YourKit, JProfiler, VisualVM) to pinpoint CPU or memory hotspots, reduce GC overhead, and quickly diagnose performance degradation.  
• High Throughput & Low Latency Applications: Designs systems that balance throughput (batch workloads) with minimal latency (real-time/near-real-time services). Applies concurrency frameworks, caching strategies (e.g., Redis), and optimizes serialization formats to improve response times.  
• Load & Stress Testing: Sets up realistic performance experiments, using JMeter, Gatling, or other tools, to stress-test applications, interpret results, and propose architectural or code-level optimizations.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Security and Compliance
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• Secure Coding Practices: Incorporates security at design-time (defensive coding, validated input, secure authentication/authorization) and run-time (monitoring suspicious activities, preventing injection attacks, etc.). Knows how to apply encryption, hashing, and secure session management.  
• Framework-Specific Security: Leverages Spring Security or Jakarta Security, configures role-based or permission-based access controls, and understands OAuth2, JWT, and SAML-based single sign-on for enterprise contexts.  
• Compliance & Standards: Guides teams to adhere to security best practices and relevant standards (OWASP Top 10, PCI-DSS, GDPR concerns regarding data handling) when writing Java-based applications.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. Mentorship, Collaboration, and Technical Leadership
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• Code Reviews & Quality Assessments: Routinely performs thorough code reviews, focusing on correctness, readability, performance, and maintainability. Mentors junior developers to improve coding style and adherence to best practices.  
• Cross-Team Collaboration: Works effectively with product owners, QA engineers, operations, and other stakeholders to align technical solutions with business requirements. Manages upstream/downstream dependencies in integrated environments.  
• Architectural Guidance: Participates in or leads architectural discussions, fosters consistent standards across teams, and ensures that system designs align with enterprise goals and constraints—balancing performance, reliability, and maintainability.
